title: A continuous functor of sites pulls sheaves back to sheaves by precomposition (Stacks 00WW)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be sites, each a site in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH: a category whose objects and morphisms form sets, with a set $\operatorname{Cov}$ of families $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ (coverings) such that every isomorphism $\{V\to U\}$ is a covering, if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i}$ and $\{V_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j}$ for every $i$ are coverings then $\{V_{ij}\to U\}_{i,j}$ is a covering, and for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and a morphism $V\to U$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ exist and $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ is a covering. A sheaf of sets (resp. of abelian groups) on a site is a presheaf $\mathcal F$ of sets (resp. abelian groups) such that for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ the diagram $\mathcal F(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer (Sites, Definitions 00VM and 00VR; [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]); morphisms are natural transformations. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a continuous functor (Sites, Definition 00WV): for every covering $\{V_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ of $\mathcal C$, (a) $\{u(V_i)\to u(V)\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$, and (b) for every morphism $T\to V$ of $\mathcal C$ the canonical morphism $u(T\times_VV_i)\to u(T)\times_{u(V)}u(V_i)$ is an isomorphism (in particular the target fibre product exists). Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal D$ the presheaf $u^p\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u$, $V\mapsto\mathcal G(u(V))$ (restriction maps $\mathcal G(u(g))$), is a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$; more precisely, for every covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ of $\mathcal C$, the sheaf condition of $u^p\mathcal G$ for $\{V_i\to V\}$ is equivalent to the sheaf condition of $\mathcal G$ for the covering $\{u(V_i)\to u(V)\}$ of $\mathcal D$, via the isomorphisms $u(V_i\times_VV_j)\cong u(V_i)\times_{u(V)}u(V_j)$ of (b). The same holds for sheaves of abelian groups: $\mathcal G\circ u$ is then a sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal C$. (Stacks Sites, Lemma 00WW.)
